interface.title: Multi-Junction RT-PCR Primer Designer (primer.py, Streamlit)
interface.field: Molecular biology / gene expression (RT-PCR, qPCR assay design)
interface.stage_of_work: Assay design before wet-lab work: designing and choosing primers, then checking specificity in silico before ordering
interface.what_it_is_for: From a genomic sequence with exons in UPPERCASE and introns in lowercase, design primer3 primer pairs whose amplicons span each exon-exon junction, so genomic DNA is not amplified. Pairs are ranked by penalty and dimer ΔG, the binding sites are mapped on the sequence, and a summary of the top-recommended pair can be downloaded before checking it in NCBI Primer-BLAST.

data.note: The provided data/sample_spliced_sequence.fasta was NOT used. The app has no upload box and the browser could not read the file. Instead I typed a test sequence by hand: 3 exons in UPPERCASE with 2 short lowercase introns, based on human GAPDH coding sequence from memory with made-up introns. The app found 2 junctions. Treat all primer sequences, sizes and ΔG values in this tree as illustrative of this hand-made input only.

tree.general: Design primer pairs whose product crosses a splice boundary, so they detect spliced transcripts but not genomic DNA, then choose the best pair and get it ready to order and validate
tree.specific: Design primer3 pairs whose amplicon spans each exon-exon junction of a case-masked sequence, choose the top-recommended pair, download its report and hand off to NCBI Primer-BLAST

children.specific: Paste a sequence with UPPERCASE exons and lowercase introns into the 'Paste sequence here' box. Introns must be lowercase: an all-uppercase input yields no junctions and nothing is designed. Preparing the case-masked input (e.g. with the companion FASTA converter the Help tab mentions) happens outside this app and was not done in this run.

children.general: Design and rank candidate primer pairs whose product crosses each boundary
children.specific: Click 'Analyze All Junctions' with default settings (2 pairs per junction, size 18–25 with optimum 20, Tm 55–65 with optimum 60, product 100–500 bp). Each junction is set as a primer3 target on the spliced template, so the amplicon spans the junction while the primers usually sit in flanking exons. An amplicon that covers one junction's target can also cover the other junction, so the same pair can be listed under both junctions.

features.name: Case-masked sequence to junction-spanning primer design
features.general: Paste a sequence whose letter case marks kept and removed regions, set design constraints, and run one batch design that returns candidates whose product crosses every boundary between kept regions
features.specific: Paste UPPERCASE exons and lowercase introns, set pairs per junction, primer size, Tm and product size in the sidebar, and press 'Analyze All Junctions' to run primer3 with each exon-exon junction as the amplicon target
steps: Paste the case-masked sequence into the text area (introns must be lowercase, or no junctions are found)
Choose how many pairs to find per junction (slider 1–5)
Set optimal/min/max primer size, Tm and min/max product size, keeping each optimum inside its min–max window
Press Analyze All Junctions
Change a setting and press Analyze again (results are not updated until you re-run)
serves_tasks: Design and rank candidate primer pairs whose product crosses each boundary
Tighten the constraints and get new candidates
Restrict to a short-amplicon (qPCR-style) product size window

features.name: Ranked candidate table with sort, search and fullscreen
features.general: Compare all candidates in one ranked table; re-sort by any metric, search for a sequence, and expand to see hidden columns
features.specific: The Global Junction Evaluation dataframe (Rank, Junction ID, Penalty Score, Cross-ΔG, Forward, Reverse, Fwd Tm, Rev Tm, Product Size), ranked by penalty then cross-ΔG, with column-header sorting, a search box and fullscreen. Its rank does not match the pair index in the junction picker.
steps: Read the table ranked by penalty
Click a column header (e.g. Cross-ΔG) to re-sort
Open search and type a primer fragment to highlight matching cells
Open fullscreen to see the Product Size column

features.name: Junction and pair picker with thermodynamic detail panel
features.general: Pick a group, then one candidate in it, and see a detail panel with each component's properties, pair-level properties and risk flags
features.specific: Choose a junction in 'Select Junction', then a pair index with the radio buttons, to show forward/reverse Tm, GC%, self-dimer ΔG with status, plus expected product size and cross-dimer ΔG. The status has only two levels in the code (Low Risk if ΔG > -9, else High Risk), so the Help tab's 'Moderate' band never appears.
steps: Open the Select Junction dropdown and choose a junction
Choose a pair index (0..n-1) with the radio buttons
Read per-primer Tm, GC% and self-dimer ΔG with Low/High status
Read Primer Pair Analysis: product size and cross-dimer ΔG
serves_tasks: Inspect each boundary's candidates one by one

features.name: Primer binding-site map on the genomic sequence
features.general: Show the selected candidate's binding sites as coloured highlights on the full annotated sequence, so you can see whether they cross region boundaries
features.specific: The Transcript-Level Primer Binding Map shows the full sequence (exons UPPERCASE, introns lowercase) with the forward primer in yellow and the reverse primer's binding site in cyan. A junction-spanning primer appears split across the intron. The map follows the junction and pair picker.
steps: Select a junction and pair in the picker
Scroll to the binding map
Check that the yellow and cyan sites sit across or around an intron (split highlight = junction-spanning primer)
Switch to another pair and compare placements
serves_tasks: Confirm where the primers bind relative to the exon/intron structure

features.name: Top recommendation card with downloadable summary
features.general: Show the single best result as a highlighted card and export that best result as a plain-text report for ordering or record-keeping
features.specific: The '🌟 Top Recommendation: Junction N' card (forward/reverse primer, Tm, GC%, self-ΔG) and the '📥 Download Detailed Summary (.txt)' button, which saves junction_N_report.txt with pair metrics (product size, Tm difference, cross-dimer ΔG and status). The export always covers the top-ranked pair, not the pair selected in the picker.
steps: Run the analysis
Read the Top Recommendation card
Press Download Detailed Summary (.txt) to save the top pair's report
Re-run with new settings and download again for the new top pair
serves_tasks: Save a text record of the top-recommended pair for ordering

features.name: Link-out to an external specificity checker
features.general: Hand the chosen pair to an external service that checks it against a genome or transcriptome for off-target products
features.specific: The sidebar '🚀 Primer BLAST Validation' button opens NCBI Primer-BLAST in a new tab; the primers are entered and checked there, outside this app
steps: Note the forward and reverse primers of the pair to validate (e.g. from the downloaded report)
Click 🚀 Primer BLAST Validation in the sidebar
Switch to the new NCBI Primer-BLAST tab
Enter the primers and run the check in NCBI (outside this app; not done in this run)
serves_tasks: Hand the pair to an external service to check its specificity

features.general: Read, inside the tool, the thresholds used to flag risky candidates
features.specific: The Help & Documentation tab (workflow steps and ΔG risk bands) together with the '📖 Terminology & Scoring Guide' expander under the results table

screens_never_reached: A friendly 'no junctions found' or 'invalid settings' message: input with no introns just cleared the results silently (screens/037.webp), and inconsistent Tm settings showed a raw OSError traceback (screens/039.webp).
not_done: Could not use data/sample_spliced_sequence.fasta: the app has no file uploader and the browser cannot read the test file's contents, so I typed in my own GAPDH-like exon/intron test sequence.
The CSV download button on the results table produced no downloaded file in this browser (tried twice, including in fullscreen).
Did not run a specificity check in NCBI Primer-BLAST: the link opened the NCBI form (screens/045.webp), but filling it in and submitting it is outside this app and the task's scope.

Could not download a report for a pair I picked myself: the summary download always saves the overall top recommendation, even when another junction or pair is selected (junction_1_report.txt was saved while Junction 2 was being viewed).
Dead end (was t4): analyzing an all-uppercase sequence (one exon, no introns) cleared the results with no message (screens/037.webp). Introns must be marked in lowercase for anything to be designed.

Crash (was t7): setting Max Tm (57.5) below Optimal Tm (60) and analyzing gave a raw 'OSError: Optimum primer Tm lower than minimum or higher than maximum' traceback from primer3 (screens/039.webp). Keep each optimum inside its min–max window.
